Ui.Script:
-- The readout has exactly three reasons to be on screen, and every function below is some -- combination of them: the Status Text option pins it (only on a bar that opted in with -- `textLockable`), the pointer is on the bar (a refcount, so nested hovers balance), or the -- bar is showing its zero text — a phrase rather than a number, which stands on its own. -- -- The option test is the one of the three that reads from outside the bar, and it is asked -- from three places, so it lives here once. It takes the option's VALUE rather than calling -- GetCVar itself: the CVAR_UPDATE handler is handed the new value along with the event and -- must not go asking the engine for the one it is being told about. local function optionPins(bar, setting) return setting == "1" and bar.textLockable end
-- `bar` is optional and falls back to `this`, the same shape TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString -- below already has (and for the same reason): the ref calls this from a bar's own OnLoad, -- where `this` is the bar, but our unit frames wire their children from ONE shared -- BenillaUnitFrame_OnLoad that holds each bar as a value, not as `this` (decision 1143). function TextStatusBar_Initialize(bar) if not bar then bar = this end bar:RegisterEvent("CVAR_UPDATE") bar.lockShow = 0 end
-- Hand a bar the FontString its readout lives in. A bar without one is never an error -- below — it simply has nothing to say, and every entry point here checks for that. function SetTextStatusBarText(bar, text) if not bar or not text then return end bar.TextString = text end
function TextStatusBar_OnEvent(cvar, value) if event ~= "CVAR_UPDATE" or cvar ~= "STATUS_BAR_TEXT" or not this.TextString then return end -- Switching the option ON pins the readout up at once. Switching it off only puts the -- readout away when nothing else is holding it there: a hover in progress keeps its own, -- and gets to hide it when it ends. if optionPins(this, value) then this.TextString:Show() elseif this.lockShow == 0 then this.TextString:Hide() end end
-- Repaint one bar's readout from the value it is currently carrying. `textStatusBar` is -- optional and falls back to `this` for the same reason TextStatusBar_Initialize's is. function TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString(textStatusBar) if not textStatusBar then textStatusBar = this end local readout = textStatusBar.TextString if not readout then return end local value = textStatusBar:GetValue() local _, valueMax = textStatusBar:GetMinMaxValues() -- No ceiling is not the same thing as a bar at zero (below): it means the bar does not -- apply to this unit at all, so the BAR leaves the screen rather than reading out a -- number. Its readout is left exactly as it stands and comes back with it. if valueMax <= 0 then textStatusBar:Hide() return end textStatusBar:Show() if value == 0 and textStatusBar.zeroText then -- Empty, and this bar has a phrase for empty. The phrase displaces the numbers and -- is shown outright: it is a message, so neither the option nor a hover gates it, -- and `isZero` is the flag that tells the hover not to take it away again. textStatusBar.isZero = 1 readout:SetText(textStatusBar.zeroText) readout:Show() return end textStatusBar.isZero = nil if textStatusBar.prefix then readout:SetText(textStatusBar.prefix .. " " .. value .. " / " .. valueMax) else readout:SetText(value .. " / " .. valueMax) end if optionPins(textStatusBar, GetCVar("statusBarText")) or textStatusBar.lockShow > 0 then readout:Show() else readout:Hide() end end
function TextStatusBar_OnValueChanged() TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString() end
function SetTextStatusBarTextPrefix(bar, prefix) if bar and bar.TextString then bar.prefix = prefix end end
function SetTextStatusBarTextZeroText(bar, zeroText) if bar and bar.TextString then bar.zeroText = zeroText end end
-- One more hold on the readout. `lockShow` counts rather than flags because two things can -- be holding it open at once: the character sheet takes a hold for as long as it is open -- (CharacterFrame_OnShow, decision 1146) and a hover on the same bar takes a second one on -- top. Only the last release puts the readout away, so the hover still balances. function ShowTextStatusBarText(bar) if bar and bar.TextString then bar.lockShow = (bar.lockShow or 0) + 1 bar.TextString:Show() end end
-- One hold released. The count floors at none rather than going negative, so an unbalanced -- release — a frame hidden out from under a hover — cannot strand the readout on screen. function HideTextStatusBarText(bar) if bar and bar.TextString then bar.lockShow = math.max((bar.lockShow or 0) - 1, 0) -- Releasing a hold only puts the readout away if none of the three reasons is left. -- The ref reads `this.isZero` for the middle one — a leak of the handler's own frame -- into a helper that otherwise takes `bar`. Equivalent at every call site (each -- caller passes its handler's own frame), so it is written as `bar`, which also -- keeps the function callable outside a handler, where `this` is nil. if bar.lockShow > 0 or bar.isZero == 1 or optionPins(bar, GetCVar("statusBarText")) then bar.TextString:Show() else bar.TextString:Hide() end end end

Scripts.OnEnter: TextStatusBar_UpdateTextString() ShowTextStatusBarText(this) if this.tooltipTitle and GameTooltip_AddNewbieTip then BenillaTooltip_AddNewbieTipFor(this, this.tooltipTitle, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, this.tooltipText, 1) end
Scripts.OnLeave: HideTextStatusBarText(this) if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:Hide() end
